items: Clean room (fresh web research + two sealed writers, prompts run verbatim): new clips for the reporter (3) and the button (5).
Shot 3: the ambulance now stays parked side-on the whole shot, while cars pass.
Shot 5: the ambulance drives straight away with its back to us. The clip turned at the junction in its first second, so the cut starts after the turn.
Ending: five real headlines slam in meme-style over the last line. Each is verbatim from the outlet's own page, retyped in our lettering with Outlet, Year. No screenshots or logos (UK fair dealing).
BadCode logo over the whole film, top left.
No UK headline: the research found no solid UK case (one shaky Baker Street story, advised against). These are from Malaysia, India and Russia. Fine, or leave the headlines out?
Overlay: logo bug only. Want more news-channel dressing (a LIVE tag, a lower-third strap)?
Still 21.9 s against the 20 s target.

replies.at205: Fixed in round 2 with a clean room: a web researcher (no repo) found that video models flip small, blurry vehicles. The fix is to keep the ambulance as a parked landmark and give the motion to one line of cars going one way. A sealed writer wrote the prompt from that brief only. The new clip pl-03-cr2A has the ambulance parked side-on throughout. New material: 1 Flow clip.
replies.at426: Fixed the same way: the new clip pl-05-cr2A has it drive straight away, rear lights toward us, getting smaller. It turned at the junction in its first second, so the shot now starts at 1.2 s and you never see the turn. New material: 1 Flow clip (the other two clean-room prompts were refused by Flow).
replies.at529: Done: five real headlines (Malay Mail 2021, News Minute 2015, Moscow Times 2016, Deccan Chronicle 2017, Daily Excelsior 2026) land one every ~0.95 s during "A politician blocking the path of an ambulance. Poetic, really..." and stack up. All verbatim, sources in research/news-stories.md. The BadCode logo sits top left for the whole film. Edit only, no credits.
